cases.title: Two hazards, fixed where they are
cases.blurb: Two flashing regions, 6 and 10 flashes a second. The model reads the measurements, picks a regional temporal low-pass with a strength computed from the measured swing, and the analyzer re-checks each candidate before it can be accepted.

cases.title: The check fails, so the model changes its plan
cases.blurb: A full-frame red strobe. The first fix comes back from the analyzer as still failing at 5.5 flashes a second; the model lowers the filter strength in response and the next candidate passes.

cases.title: Stops and asks a person
cases.blurb: The same clip under the deterministic policy: the candidate that passes changes the picture too much to accept automatically, so the job pauses until a person approves or rejects it. Both outcomes are recorded.

limits: It checks published thresholds as implemented here; a pass is not a certification and not medical advice. Threshold tests have known misses: a 2024 UK TV ad that passed the Harding test was still pulled after viewers reported seizures.

Luminance is relative to peak white (sRGB curve). On the Ofcom note's reference display (gamma 2.2, 200 cd/m² peak white) its 20 and 160 cd/m² limits are exactly our 0.10 and 0.80; a brighter real display is not modelled.
The area rule runs on a 64x48 grid, so a hazard right at the 25% boundary can flip with grid size (1 of 28 boundary clips at some grid sizes).
A full-frame strobe has no regional fix: the repair has to change the whole picture, and when it changes it too much the job waits for a person.
The pattern detector (regular stripes) is experimental and off by default; the WCAG exemption for fine balanced patterns is not implemented, so it over-flags rather than under-flags.
External ground truth is small: 18 third-party clips, no labelled concert or emergency-vehicle footage yet.
